unresolved.evidence: Nominal arithmetic is correct: both gate judges are 600s (their judge.toml:4), so 600+600=1200 < gates 1500; scored judges are 9000/900/900s (their judge.toml:4), so 10800 < scored 11100. tests/test.sh:207 serializes judges with --max-concurrent-agent 1; suite calls at 213 and 224 give 1500+11100=12600 < task.toml:27 verifier 13200, leaving 600s outside suites. All judge maxima total 12000 < 13200. Agent 7200s and build 600s at task.toml:18,21 match the frozen template. However, the whole lifecycle is not bounded by those inner allowances: tests/test.sh:33-39 cleanup sends TERM and then executes `wait "$APP_PID"` with no deadline or KILL escalation before ensure_reward. These exact bytes equal frozen template tests/test.sh (SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa). The indexed local/shared-harness-witness.py:12,47-65 uses a SIGTERM-ignoring HTTP fixture, executes unchanged test.sh, and substitutes only an external rewardkit stub that immediately exits 7. local/shared-harness/results.json:27-31,45-46 records 12.004534760984825s, entrypoint_still_running=true, the original responding PID 95, and LOCAL CLI FAILURE FIXTURE, NO GRADING. Thus the run confirms cleanup remains blocked after an already-completed grading command; source establishes there is no finite inner cleanup deadline. It does not demonstrate a complete 13200s timeout or a provider score. Verified index hashes: driver 44b58bdf8477e2e8992988b164f62691b15f55bc219cae791056b131cd5c72e6, result f77ed93b2d18771474a8624c01db1bc5c02320a5776ca1561e633d68d0beaf3f, raw log 64ef9fb6d1bb872ca54e8daf691e95a9fe9e062bfb74f2d38fd66dd22f66f2ce; every source binding in that index entry matches frozen task bytes. Separately, workload fit is NOT EXERCISED: 86 functional, 14 polish and 6 visual criteria and the functional P0-P10 browser protocols have no full configured judge duration. configured-inspection/results.json (verified SHA256 6bf9aa47913875f44e0c4b16c35169eaa2d42a6d491ce59fc4898c414cb6facc) and inspect-configured.py:22-23 only launch /usr/bin/true with argument bytes, plus CLI version commands. The 7312ms MCP result is five tool-feasibility observations, not a judge run. agent-build.log:29,33 and verifier-build.log:35-62 show cached package/browser layers, so they do not establish cold-build fit under 600s. No target-agent build duration is supplied, and runtime-evidence.json is absent. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:25-31 prohibits inferring fit from allowances or scripted probes. Initial liveness also includes two 2s per-request limits plus up to 120 quarter-second retry sleeps (test.sh:48-50,116-122), so its attempt count must not be reported as a measured fixed 30s duration. No budget change is justified by these observations.
unresolved.counterexample: Measured broken fixture: an HTTP-only server installs process.on("SIGTERM",()=>{}). Even with the grading stub already failed, the entrypoint cannot finish cleanup and remains alive at the 12s observation; the source wait has no upper bound, so this mechanism can consume the outer verifier allowance regardless of the valid suite sums. It was not observed to pass a product judge. A conforming alternative with all required persistent product behavior but a graceful-shutdown handler that leaves an active connection or background drain running can hit the same unbounded wait; the public instruction and integration contract do not impose a signal-shutdown deadline. Separately, a conforming implementation may need more UI discovery and control setup than the scripted golden; without a full configured run, its 86-row functional review can exhaust 9000s and lose unobserved credit (functional/prompt.md:9). This latter timing risk remains hypothetical, not a measured overrun.
unresolved.suggested_fix: Escalate the canonical cleanup defect to the shared-harness owner for an authorized bounded TERM/grace/KILL/reap correction, then freeze the corrected candidate and collect hash-bound full configured judge, target-builder and cold-build timing evidence before clearance; preserve current budgets unless measured workload justifies an explicitly authorized change below five hours.

Frozen task/tests/test.sh and frozen template/tests/test.sh have the identical SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa. The normal wiring is sound: lines 60-61 prewrite zero and install EXIT cleanup; lines 68-83 reject missing entry/escaping symlinks; lines 104-125 launch with env -i, uid/gid 65534 and probe liveness; lines 213-227 run gates, score.py, then scored and score.py. However cleanup sends only SIGTERM and executes unbounded `wait "$APP_PID"` at lines 36-37, before ensure_reward at line 39. Independently inspected shared-harness-witness.py:12,47-67 runs the exact entrypoint with a responsive server ignoring SIGTERM and a local rewardkit stub exiting 7. Hash-verified shared-harness/results.json:26-46 records entrypoint_still_running=true after 12.0045 seconds and the same PID 95 still answering. Source shows no deadline or escalation, so this path can consume the outer verifier budget. Crucially reward=0, graded=0, no_op=1 already existed (results.json:32-44 and cleanup/reward.json); this is NOT a demonstrated missing-reward or completed-score-loss defect. The generated restart helper has the related lifecycle problem at test.sh:152-178: after its bounded TERM wait it launches without confirming the old group exited, then treats any listener as ready. The raw restart log contains EADDRINUSE for replacement PID 68 while results.json:5-24 reports successful MCP restart and original PID 7 still answering. I independently reconstructed the helper from the frozen heredoc and matched the runtime helper exactly. All indexed shared-harness artifact hashes and all source bindings in that index entry match current files; results SHA256 f77ed93b2d18771474a8624c01db1bc5c02320a5776ca1561e633d68d0beaf3f, driver SHA256 44b58bdf8477e2e8992988b164f62691b15f55bc219cae791056b131cd5c72e6. These are no-provider fixture observations, not full configured grading or measured reward impact.
unresolved.counterexample: A responsive submission with `process.on("SIGTERM",()=>{})` prevents cleanup from completing after a failed gate CLI; this exact lifecycle behavior is measured. A broken app with RAM-only records and that handler can keep the original state through the falsely successful restart, making hro_restart (functional/judge.toml:789-794) observe matching records without a real process restart; the helper false success is measured, while criterion credit is an inference and was not run. Conversely, an otherwise conforming SQLite app whose shutdown handler leaves the listener alive can hang finalization despite satisfying the public product/runtime contract, which does not impose SIGTERM behavior. A real configured judge score or portal outcome is not claimed.
unresolved.suggested_fix: Escalate to the shared-template owner for an authorized upstream lifecycle fix: preserve/ensure reward before bounded cleanup, escalate termination if needed, confirm the old group has exited and the new process owns the live server before restart success; adopt a new frozen candidate after approval rather than editing canonical shared files locally.

The template tests/test.sh is byte-identical (SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa); the frozen template integration note also omits cwd, so this is inherited, not task-specific harness drift. unresolved.counterexample: Conforming alternative: an otherwise correct Express/SQLite app honors PORT and DB_PATH, copies seed data into /app, exposes database-independent /api/health, and loads its bundled seed/UI with fs.readFileSync('seed_data.json') or express.static('public'). It works when node /app/server.js is invoked in the supplied /app working directory, yet the unchanged verifier's /tests cwd makes those relative lookups fail. The undisclosed cwd, rather than missing requested product behavior, can cause zero render credit. Broken-app challenge: a health-only or HTTP-500 server passes test.sh's permissive readiness probe (48-55), but render/judge.toml:23 requires a successful authenticated populated workspace and constraints/judge.toml:23-25 requires real creation plus independent readback, so readiness alone is not an overall-pass loophole and is not reported as a separate defect.
unresolved.suggested_fix: Preserve the canonical harness; add the actual launch conditions to the task's public integration note, including that cwd is not /app and bundled assets must resolve from the entry/module directory or explicit absolute paths, then freeze and review the changed candidate.

unresolved.evidence: Requirement-to-criterion mapping substantially covers the ask: login/identity -> hro_gate_render/hro_accounts; shared durable creation -> hro_gate_shared/hro_readback/hro_restart; seed -> seven hro_seed_* rows; IDs and creation -> hro_req_identity/hro_offer_identity/hro_duplicate_identity and unusual-ID lifecycle rows; validation -> P2 rows; composition/bands -> hro_compensation_breakdown/hro_intrinsic/hro_annual/hro_runrate/hro_basis/hro_bands; roles, dual control and budgets -> P5/P6 rows; approval/revision/rescission effects, history, vesting, referral and concurrency -> P4/P7/P8/P9 rows; dashboard -> hro_dashboard; accessibility, themes, recovery and states -> Polish; visual quality -> six anchored Visual rows. Shared flows are allowed by Internal Quality Checks!E27; no finding is based merely on bundled rules. Two uncovered promises remain. (1) .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/task/environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md:260-263 explicitly requires replacing the active grant with revised "unit count, fair value and strike price". .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:443 checks revised units, original instant, historical status/cancellations and zero-unit removal, but never the replacement grant fair/strike values. hro_revision_lineage at :398 checks the six economic fields of the OFFER; hro_grant at :362 checks units/date/schedule; neither establishes replacement GRANT prices. P4 in functional/prompt.md changes fair/strike on the offer but supplies no scored comparison of these replacement-grant prices. (2) .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/task/environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md:370-383 and :401-402 requires all action identity/permissions to come from session and all documented optional claims to be ignored. .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:605 applies claimedActorId/claimedRole/claimedTier only to approval; :614 checks approval economic claims; :623 checks only claimedClawbackCents/claimedCancelledUnits on rescission. functional/prompt.md:49 explicitly limits the claim controls to those approval and rescission bodies. Revision has no claim probe, and nonapproval creation/rescission have no forged identity/role probe. Ordinary wrong-role controls (:290/:299), anonymous-family controls and normal audit actor checks do not exercise a caller adding these claims. Hash verification found zero mismatches across all 69 frozen task/rules files. The raw-evidence-index.json was absent when read; no browser, mutation or configured judge run was performed for this row. These are bounded source coverage counterexamples, not an empirical score or a claim about the golden. Shared template implementation constraints were distinguished from task-specific browser criteria; this finding does not ask for source-reading or a database-engine browser probe.
unresolved.counterexample: Broken app A correctly revises all six offer fields and computes every budget/vesting amount from the offer, but copies the original grant prices (fair 1.02, strike .01) onto the B and C replacement grants instead of B 2.03/.02 and C 3.04/.03. It keeps correct 11/13 units, start, historical status and cancellation counts. All specified observations for hro_revision_lineage, hro_revision_equity, compensation and settlement can still pass, while the explicit replacement-grant promise fails. Broken app B ignores all claims during approval, and ignores claimedClawbackCents/claimedCancelledUnits during rescission, but its revision/rescission handler chooses permission actor as claimedActorId or claimedRole when supplied, falling back to the valid session otherwise. All unmodified role tests and the existing claim tests pass, yet an Auditor can submit an observed valid rescission/revision body with Finance/Recruiter identity claims and change the books. An implementation that rejects optional claims only on revision similarly escapes the current claim controls despite the explicit ignore requirement. Conforming-alternative check: a page-based UI with generated revision IDs, semantic actor names and equivalent dollar/UTC representations can satisfy the existing criteria; no coverage-related false-fail was established. A fix must allow normal UI/product response associations and observed request formats, rather than introduce grant field names, routes or layouts.
unresolved.suggested_fix: In a new candidate, add explicit replacement-grant fair/strike comparisons to the existing P4 grant observation (including preserved historical values), and extend bounded optional-claim/session-authority probes to the remaining observed action families with successful omission controls and independently owned credit; preserve ordinary request schemas, public requirements and shared harness policy.

unresolved.evidence: The authoritative workbook Quality Checks!D29 forbids duplicate/subsumed criteria; the internal annotation permits sharing a flow, not double credit ownership. Current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:13 further requires preserving independently useful observations. Two concrete conflicts remain. (1) .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:605 (hro_claim_identity, weight 1.0) adds claimedActorId, claimedRole AND claimedTier and requires an otherwise valid request to have the same result as omission. The same file:614 (hro_claim_approval_economics, weight 0.5) adds claimedBand, claimedTier AND claimedCommittedCents, again requiring the optional claims to be ignored and explicitly failing rejection merely for their presence. The valid-approval acceptance of claimedTier is therefore the same observable graded twice; no ownership/fallback rule isolates it. Public environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md:380-383 requires ignoring these keys but does not make ignoring one key two independent outcomes. (2) tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:110 explicitly limits hro_offer_identity to creation/saved identity and gives later unusual-ID approval/rescission/revision routing separate owners; lines119 and128 separately own unusual-ID approval and rescission. But tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:34 commands, after performing approval and subsequent actions on unusual IDs, "If ID routing fails, retain that failure in hro_offer_identity". This assigns a later routing miss to the already-proven creation outcome and conflicts with both its criterion boundary and prompt.md:9 independent scoring. Counterexamples below establish textual scoring defects; no provider run or empirical judge deduction was executed. Static hash verification matched all 69 frozen task/rule files and the current policy to the manifest for adb13696bfe3e6c71690adc5c6af2002d5f107a10751c348ba8bc0f5401600b1. No raw-evidence index was present, and this report does not claim an Oracle, model, portal or full-judge result. Reviewed non-defects: ordinary positive controls, refusal plus unchanged financial state, and shared setup are coherent outcomes under policy; the explicit separation of feedback/enforcement, arithmetic/history, anonymous write families, same-target concurrency and mobile operability/visual composition generally preserves credit. Tried seed-only/no-op storage as a broken-pass candidate: the required unique UI creation plus independent Auditor readback prevents that witness by the written gate. Tried conforming nonmodal editors, stacked/scrollable breakdowns, native date controls, opaque routes and a common bootstrap response: the wording permits these alternatives; no fully conforming-app false-fail is asserted for them.
unresolved.counterexample: A: An otherwise functional app ignores all optional keys except that a validator rejects the presence of claimedTier on an authorized approval. Omission controls approve normally; role enforcement, stored actor, band, commitment and headroom are correct. The same isolated claimedTier defect fails both hro_claim_identity and hro_claim_approval_economics, even though claimedBand/claimedCommittedCents protection works. B: An app correctly stores and retrieves unusual requisition/offer IDs and every entered field but forgets URL encoding only in its approval handler; ordinary-ID approval works. P1 creation/readback satisfies hro_offer_identity, while hro_offer_id_lifecycle correctly fails. Repeating that same routing miss in P4 makes prompt.md:34 assign failure to hro_offer_identity as well, erasing independently valid creation credit. These are source-level partial-app counterexamples, not claimed executed mutations.
unresolved.suggested_fix: Give claimedTier acceptance/authority exactly one criterion owner (for example retain it in identity and test approval economics with only claimedBand/claimedCommittedCents), and change P4 to record each routing failure only against its actual action-specific owner while preserving saved creation/readback credit; explicitly assign revision-ID routing if needed and keep the ordinary-ID fallback for unrelated economic outcomes.
